ok.description: Whether the declarations were accepted into the fork.

AtomChange.description:
One changed atom in a derived-consequence diff: the ground atom and its
standing before (base) and after (fork), with a rendered one-line summary.

after.description: Its standing under the fork's candidate valuation.

atom.description: The ground atom whose standing changed.

before.description: Its standing under the base ledger.

rendered.description: A rendered one-line summary of the change.

ConflictKind.description:
The kind of a conflict, naming the three ways forks (and a fork against the
ledger) can disagree (spec 02 §5, the merge constraint-join):

oneOf.description: Two sides valuate the same event variable differently.

The joined valuation violates `Θ` — two options of one exclusivity
family are ruled true together.

The joined certain layers break a functional dependency or a
`C`-constraint; the blame pair is the two monomials that cannot co-hold.

DiffConflict.description: A conflict carried by either a fork diff or a Door-T staged-world diff.

blame.description: The claims, assignments, or findings that cannot co-hold.

code.description: Stable finding code for machine routing.

kind.description: Fork conflict family, when the conflict comes from the fork engine.

DiffDelta.description: A derived-consequence diff delta, shared by the fork mutation ops.

conflicts.description: Typed conflicts surfaced by the delta.

grade_changed.description: Atoms whose grade changed, with before/after standing and rendering.

newly_certain.description: Atoms that became certain, with before/after standing and rendering.

newly_dead.description: Atoms that became dead, with before/after standing and rendering.

newly_possible.description: Atoms that became merely possible, with before/after standing and rendering.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

GroundAtom.description:
A ground atom: a predicate applied to fully-ground argument renderings. This
is the identity of a fact or a derived tuple in the relation.

args.description: The ground argument renderings, in order.

Standing.description:
A claim's standing in one world under one valuation: its three-valued status
and its grade. `before`/`after` pairs of these are the atoms of a diff.

grade.description: The grade at which the claim is known.

status.description: The claim's three-valued status (a dead or absent atom reads `dead`).

Status.description: A claim's three-valued standing under `(ν, Θ)`, derived — never stored.

oneOf.description:
Every monomial is `Θ`-unsatisfiable: the claim holds in no admissible
world. (Whether this is rejection or mere supersession is a `C`
question, outside the algebra.)

Some monomial is `Θ`-satisfiable but none is resolved-and-undefeated: the
shadow layer.

Some monomial holds on resolved events alone, with that monomial's own
defeater not fully ruled: assertable.
